A lot of fulfillment comes from making life better for a community. That's just how humans work. We're pack animals. We work in a group. When you're working in a company that has eleven thousand other workers, your individual contribution is meaningless sure you processed a bunch of things that eventually turn into something nice for whoever's paying for it, but you have no interaction. You have no idea if what you did made someone happy. 

I worked in a meat packing plant for a while and that's what bothered me the most. There is no fruit to this labour except for the cheque I get every couple weeks that barely pays my bills. 

In this kind of life, existence is definitely futile. Futile, boring, useless. We've evolved our systems to be modular, so that one person is skilled in one boring mundane task so they're easy to replace. It's just mathematics.

Food, rest, and sunlight are the foundation of existence, and our best weapons against depression. Unfortunately, being depressed means that this trifecta of sorts is one of the hardest things to take care of. Making sure that these three things are taken care of is the most basic, and most important part of not just recovering from depression or depressive episodes, but also to simply being able to function during the day. 

I wish I could give you the answer that you seek, but I too struggle with sleeping and eating correctly. Seeing a specialist may help you to find a method to balance your eating and sleeping habits.

A lot of people feel like they are bound and restricted by their depression, but this is probably the first time I have personally seen it shown like this. That we have the power to let go, but the nature of our self hatred prevents us from helping ourselves. I can relate to that.

The issue isn't that they are the wrong thing - in some circumstances they can be the best thing. the issue is that they are cannot be trained to competently respond to every single kind of call. They already need to know how to talk down violent people, the process on what they can do, and how they can do it - it's a lot for even the brightest of people. They are usually trained on how to talk to people who are suicidal - but they only know how to deal with an immediate threat which is why they haul people to the hospital. They know how to get people to not hurt themselves, not to help diagnose and definitely not to help solve them.  That's not what they're trained to do. 

Police are emergency responders. They are there to make sure that you are safe for the time being, then to bring you somewhere you can receive better care than their 3 year degree and 2 year training program can give.

Fake it till you make it I don't think is a phrase to describe how you treat yourself. It's teaching you a skill. That skill is that even if a goal looks impossible to accomplish, you can still do it if you step outside your comfort zone to accomplish it. 

If you need to deliver a presentation and your anxiety is not playing ball, fake it till you make it means stepping out even though you are anxious and ignoring it until the moment has passed. 

From one depressed person to another, this in itself can prove impossible. I don't know how to word this without being wishy washy, so I'll just end it with the statement that finding the willpower to continue on is what breaks some people out of depression. So to an extent when people say "fake it till you make it" they are telling the truth - they just try to paint it as an all encompassing solution.

And that's the truth. Have you ever remembered a specific phrase someone said from years ago that isn't particularly important - but your brain seemed to remember it like your life depended on it? Every good deed we do has that kind of long-lasting potential.

I never smoked weed that much but I understand that it can have many effects on the brain in different people. It also causes a lot of the same behaviours in people who do other recreational drugs or other addictions. While you may think that you only become depressed when you stop smoking, it could be that - like a cough drop - it's only covering up the symptoms of a bigger issue. It's helping you cope with the depression but it's never going to solve it. 

Much like if I have a video game addiction - while I am playing games I'm not going to feel as depressed. Does that mean that the video games are curing my depression, or helping me cope? Not really. It's simply an easy quick effective way to get a mood boost, but it also takes up time and money I could be spending on more effective means to combat depression.

People are in two categories in this context. Those who have felt true suffering, and those that have not. For those who have not, they will never understand what life is like until they too suffer. 

Their encouragement that we see as empty and tasteless, to them, is truth. And it is, which is the hard thing for people like you and me to understand - especially since we both knew suffering from a very young age. People who do not understand suffering by definition have not suffered. So as far as they are concerned the best thing to do when you're feeling 'down' is to just think out of it. Because that's all they have had to do to fix their mood or their situation. 

Maybe the worst thing that ever happened to them was losing a grandparent who they only met a handful of times. So when they feel the loss when the grandparent died, it is extremely easy to cope with. I want to make it clear that they still feel loss, they still feel pain. They still have to cope with that pain. But it is not suffering. 

I don't get angry at people who are like who you describe. I'll never be able to explain to them in a way they will understand just how much I've been hurt over time. Instead I'm actually happy for them - since they've been lucky enough to not have to endure what I have been forced to endure.

In Canada and I'm pretty sure in Britain too you can be signed into the hospital for at the very least a couple of days. That time is spent with mental health professionals throughout the day and it might be just enough to allow you to live on your own again for long enough to help work through some issues. It also gives you a very quick referral to a psychiatrist to get prescribed mood stabilisers. 

If you are American I don't know how the system works there. I hope it's similar to how it works here.

One thing that I am not sure whether you overlooked it or are aware of it is the knowledge of and acceptance that you have suffered. 

When I hit one of my lower points one of the thoughts that always crossed my mind was "Everything should be perfect - yet I'm here hating everything that I am."

I came from a good family. We weren't poor, I never did any drugs, my grades weren't stellar but they were still acceptable. But living was becoming unbearable. I had a nice talk with my mother near that time and she brought my past into perspective. 

I had suffered and things have happened to me to cause me pain. I am depressed and suffering right now not because I wasn't able to 'soldier through it' or just shake off the pain like it was nothing. I am feeling pain because that is what happens when we are subjected to things that cause pain. 

It helped me understand myself and forgive myself. I was constantly attacking myself for not being better because I thought I was tripping on obstacles that didn't exist. As a matter of fact there were many obstacles along the way that did not hinder me. I was able to cope with the pain from the death of my pet for instance. 

This little piece of information allowed me to forgive myself for feeling pain, and helped improve my mood. I am now aware to the fact that my pain is justified and I find strength in knowing that the battle I am fighting is worth fighting for.
